4. **github-app-api-compat.md repository_dispatch permission (P2, verified)** — the `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dispatches` bullet (~line 198) says auth requirement `actions: write`. github.com requires `contents: write` for repository dispatch (workflow dispatch requires `actions: write`). Update the bullet to `contents: write` and add a sibling note under the workflow-dispatch bullet if it exists stating `actions: write`. Also update any "verify" note in that area per the verified fact. The code change landing in parallel makes `authorize_workflow_dispatch` require `actions: write` and `authorize_repository_dispatch` require `contents: write` — the doc must state exactly that.
5. **github-app-webhook.md startup read-back overclaims (P3) + bootstrap.rs fix** — the doc (~line 33-42) says "At startup preloop reads an existing App's subscription back from GitHub ... and warns loudly", but bootstrap.rs (~line 480-492) only does this for the LEGACY App (`state.github_app`), never for additional `github.apps` registry entries. Fix the CODE so the claim holds: in bootstrap.rs, after the existing legacy read-back spawn, add a loop over `state.github_apps.as_ref().map(|r| &r.apps)` — for each registry App (id + pem), spawn a task that signs the App JWT (`crate::github_app::sign_app_jwt(&app.app_id, &app.private_key)` — check its exact signature/visibility in github_app.rs; it is used by `read_app_events_at(api_base, app_id, private_key)`, a pub(crate) free function that already exists) and calls `crate::github_app::read_app_events_at(crate::github::github_api_base(), &app.app_id, &private_key)` then `warn_missing_trigger_events(&app.app_id, &events)`, warning on error like the legacy branch. Reuse the existing patterns; if `AppConfig` lacks a parsed `private_key` field (it stores `pem: String`), parse the PEM the same way the registry loader does (check how `GitHubApps`/`GitHubAppCredentials` parse `pem` in github_app.rs — likely `rsa::RsaPrivateKey::from_pkcs1_pem` or similar; mirror that). If parsing in bootstrap.rs is awkward, add a small pub(crate) helper in github_app.rs that takes `&crate::config::AppConfig` and returns the events (reusing `read_app_events_at`), and call it from bootstrap.rs. Keep the doc text as-is once the code covers every configured App.

- Do NOT run cargo. Report per item: exact changes.

All five review items fixed in /Users/bnjoroge/preloop-gh-app-api-compat (head b4c00985). No cargo run (per constraint); changes verified by reading code/doc state. Item 5's doc text left as-is per instructions.

1. github-tokens.md section order (P3) — MOVED. `## 7. Dispatch API authentication` (formerly lines 298-325, heading through last line before EOF) now sits immediately before `## Related`; Related is terminal. Removed the Related block from before §7 and re-appended it at EOF with the standard `---` separator, so the numbered flow reads §1-§6 → §7 → Related. Nothing renumbered; §7 content byte-identical.

2. github-app-api-compat.md status header (P3) — UPDATED. `Status: Plan (implementation start)` → `Status: Implemented (M1–M4 per Implementation Log; M5 pending)`; `Author: design session` → `Author: design session — see §11 for the implementation record` (kept minimal; branch line untouched). M5-pending appended since the Implementation Log explicitly marks M5 as NOT done.

3. github-app-api-compat.md D2 actor contradiction (P3) — FIXED. The D2 'Actor resolution for the synthesized sender' block (it did already cover actors) now matches M3 and the code in dispatch_auth.rs: installation token → `{app_slug}[bot]` with third-party online fallback to `{account.login}[bot]` when slug absent and offline mint-ledger path using the ledger's account login; added own-App JWT → `{slug}[bot]` (`GET /app`, cached) or `{app_id}[bot]` offline; PAT → `GET /user` (cached) or `preloop-pat`; system bearer → `preloop-system`. NOTE: the task brief said 'the ledger fast path now resolves the App slug' — the code does NOT do that: dispatch_auth.rs:235-236 formats `{account_login}[bot]` from the ledger entry (account_login = repo owner set at mint time, github_app.rs:678), and the ledger lookup only consults `state.github_app`. I followed the code (per 'consistent with what M2/M3 and the code do'); the D2 bullet reflects it.

4. github-app-api-compat.md repository_dispatch permission (P2) — FIXED. §5 `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dispatches` auth bullet: `actions: write` → `contents: write` with '(github.com requires `contents: write` for repository dispatch; verified against the installation's granted permissions)'. Workflow-dispatch bullet: existing `actions: write` requirement kept and given the github.com sibling note '(github.com requires `actions: write` for workflow dispatch)'. Also updated D2 online-path line 'Require `actions: write` ... for dispatch' → 'Require the endpoint's permission in the installation's granted permissions (`actions: write` for workflow dispatch, `contents: write` for repository dispatch)' so the doc states exactly what dispatch.rs does (`authorize_workflow_dispatch`→`has_actions_write`, `authorize_repository_dispatch`→`has_contents_write`, verified present in this worktree).

5. github-app-webhook.md read-back overclaim + bootstrap.rs (P3) — CODE FIXED, doc kept as-is. bootstrap.rs serve() now spawns the `read_app_events`/`warn_missing_trigger_events` read-back for every additional registered App, after the existing legacy branch. Implementation: `if let Some(registry) = state.github_apps.as_ref()` loop over `registry.apps.iter().enumerate()`, skipping `default_index` (the legacy `state.github_app` branch above already covers the default App — state.rs derives `github_app` from `registry.default_app()`, so each App is read back exactly once; a naive all-apps loop would read the default twice and duplicate the warning). Each spawned task clones the `GitHubAppCredentials` and calls the existing `app.read_app_events().await` method — equivalent to the brief's `read_app_events_at(github_api_base(), &app_id, &private_key)` (it wraps exactly that with the same PRELOOP_GITHUB_API_URL base, and is the pattern the legacy branch already uses); PEM parsing is unnecessary because `GitHubApps.apps` holds `GitHubAppCredentials` with a parsed `rsa::RsaPrivateKey`, not `config::AppConfig`. Warning-on-error mirrors the legacy branch verbatim. No new imports (tokio::spawn, tracing warn! via `use super::*`); all accessed fields/methods (`github_apps`, `apps`, `default_index`, `read_app_events`, `warn_missing_trigger_events`) are pub(crate) in the same crate. With this, the doc claim ('At startup preloop reads an existing App's subscription back ... and warns loudly') holds for every configured App, so the doc text stays as-is.
